advisor.name: Mrs. Smith
advisor.note: Our advisor supports student leadership while encouraging cultural understanding and global citizenship.

welcome.text: We started this club because we wanted a space where curiosity about China — the food, the language, the festivals, the memes — was welcome, whether or not you speak a word of Mandarin. No experience required. Just bring your appetite and an open mind.

mission: Chinese Culture Club exists to introduce students to the richness of Chinese language, history, traditions, and modern life — through food, festivals, and friendships, not lectures.

festivals.name: Chinese New Year
festivals.note: Red envelopes, fireworks, and a reunion dinner that never seems to end.

festivals.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
festivals.note: Family, mooncakes, and staring at the same moon as people across the world.

festivals.name: Dragon Boat Festival
festivals.note: Rice dumplings and dragon boat races to honor an ancient poet.

food.name: Hot Pot
food.note: A bubbling pot everyone shares — DIY dinner and a social event in one.

food.name: Xiaolongbao
food.note: Soup dumplings. Bite a small hole first, or regret it.

food.name: Bubble Tea
food.note: Originated in Taiwan, now everywhere — yes, we have opinions on toppings.

food.name: Mala Tang
food.note: Pick your skewers, pick your spice level, proceed with caution.

funFacts.q: How many pandas live only in China?
funFacts.a: Nearly all wild giant pandas — their only natural habitat is a handful of mountain ranges in China.
Red is linked to fire and joy in Chinese tradition, and thought to scare off bad luck.

funFacts.q: How long is China's high-speed rail network?
funFacts.a: Over 40,000 km — the longest in the world, and still growing.

faqs.a: No. Everyone is welcome, no matter your background.
